_about: Allow-list for chrome_colour_check.php. A colour literal may appear in css/engcalcs.css only inside the token block, or inside a rule listed here. Every entry says why it is DATA or PAPER rather than chrome. Add an entry only for that reason; a button, box, border or text colour belongs in the token block.

css_rules.reason: map symbology: the colours that MEAN something (fire-flow verdicts, the override amber and grey, the pending red). The paper, the network ink, the lettering, the halo and the selection are --ec-map-* tokens that follow the theme on screen and print as Light (Task 811 round 3, dev/themes-plan.md)
map symbology: a Shape, the user's own drawn annotation (Task 779); its default ink is the --ec-map-shape token
map symbology: the drawing's own ink
map symbology: vertex handle drawn on the map
map symbology: the drag/move flash on a node, drawn in the drawing's red (the dark beat is --ec-map-ink)
an example thumbnail keeps its own white paper in every theme (a picture of a drawing); the words that sit on the map's paper take the --ec-map-* tokens
map symbology: the drawing's paper, --lpn-map-bg, which is the --ec-map-paper token
a swatch reports a data colour and carries its own hairline; the scale bar and the colour legend panel are themed chrome and use tokens
paper is always black on white

css_custom_properties.reason: map symbology colours, published for the drawing

inline_ratchet._about: Colour literals in the PHP pages' chrome (inline style writes). Counted per file; a count may fall, never rise. js/*.js is NOT counted here: every literal in it must match a js_literals entry below (file + line pattern + reason). js/lpn-ramps.js is colour-ramp DATA and is exempt.

_notes.Looped-Network.php: one comment (the map canvas's paper and frame are tokens since Task 811 round 3)
_notes.Branched-Network.php: legend keys that match the drawn sketch layers (data colours)
_notes.lib/*.php: web-manifest and meta theme colours, which must be literals

js_literals._about: A colour literal in js/*.js may appear only on a line matching one of these (file, regex on the line, reason). Everything else, a box, button, banner, table or menu, writes var(--ec-*). Keyed on line content, not number, so a neighbouring branch moving code does not break it.
